recap: Joel Ziehme scored with one second left, on a pass from Kyle Swogger after a steal, to give Luther a 49–47 win in the season opener. Brad Skaer, a former Luther student, scored 32 points with four 3-pointers and 10 rebounds, but fouled out just after his last 3 put Bangor ahead 47–44, and Bangor didn't score again.

Brad Skaer scored 40 points, going 6 for 8 from 3-point range and 12 for 13 at the free-throw line, as Bangor opened the Scenic Bluffs season with a win. (Wonewoc-Center's quarter scores after the first can't be read in the clipping.)

Brad Skaer scored 36 points with three 3-pointers, giving him 32, 40 and 36 in Bangor's first three games, and Chris Chandler had 11 points and 11 rebounds as Bangor led the whole game. New Lisbon held Brad Skaer, who came in averaging 36 points a game, to six points through three quarters while building a 47–33 lead. Skaer scored 17 in the fourth for a team-high 23, but it was too late. Troy Bolcerek scored 12 in his first game of the season after spraining his ankle, and New Lisbon's David Paradise led all scorers with 26.

recap: Auburndale, coached by 1963 Bangor graduate Tim Anderson, scored the first five points and never trailed. The Apaches led 28–23 at halftime, then opened the second half on a 19–8 run, with Dan Weinfurter scoring eight of his 16 in the third quarter. Auburndale held the ball for nearly three minutes on one fourth-quarter possession and kept Bangor scoreless over the final 58 seconds. Brad Skaer, averaging about 30 points, was held to 17, nine of them in the fourth, and Troy Bolcerek added 16.

Bangor handed Cashton its first Scenic Bluffs loss, holding the Eagles without a field goal in the second quarter, which Bangor won 13–5. Cashton's only points that quarter came at the free-throw line, where it went 11 for 21 for the game. Brad Skaer led Bangor with 12 points and 8 rebounds, Kyle Schroeder added 11, and Troy Bolcerek had 6 points and 4 assists.

A meeting of former coaching colleagues: first-year West Salem coach Don Addington led Bangor's program from 1984 to 1998 with Joe Stekel as his top assistant, and he still taught at Bangor High School. Dustin Wehrs scored 24 and Addington's son Ben 16, going 6 for 6 at the line, as West Salem made 16 of 22 free throws. Brad Skaer scored 30 points with 11 rebounds, his fourth 30-point game of the season, and Troy Bolcerek's desperation shot at the end hit the backboard and rimmed out.
Royall broke open a battle of second-place Scenic Bluffs teams with a 23-point third quarter. Sam Overlien led Royall with 19, and Brad Skaer had a game-high 21 for Bangor.
Troy Bolcerek's shot with 5.2 seconds left won it. G-E-T led 49–47 going into the fourth quarter.
Bolcerek scored 14 of his 19 points in the first half, and Bangor led 29–24 at halftime. Chris Chandler had 17 points and 17 rebounds.
Kyle Schroeder had three steals for breakaway layups in the third quarter, as Bangor went on a 13–4 run to put the game away.

The game was tied 14–14 at halftime, and Bangor led 21–17 after three quarters. Fourth-quarter 3-pointers from Kyle Schroeder and Brandon Meyer held off Royall, and Bangor went into the Christmas break 5–0.

The game was tied 32–32 at halftime, but Bangor outscored Hillsboro 24–7 in the third quarter to stay perfect at 9–0. Troy Bolcerek scored 17 of his 24 points in the second half. Hillsboro's Greg Jefferies led all scorers with 26.

source: Coulee News and La Crosse Tribune clippings
recap: Bangor opened with a 16–0 run and led 19–2 after one quarter, hitting four of its 10 3-pointers in the first. West Salem cut it to 48–35 after three, but Bangor won the fourth 22–14 and went 20 of 23 from the free-throw line to reach 10–0.

Lukas Ermis, Kyle Schroeder, Brandon Meyer and Eddie Ikert hit consecutive 3-pointers for a 26–13 lead early in the second quarter, and Cashton got no closer than 13 after Bangor went up 35–17. Troy Bolcerek, playing on an ankle he injured three days earlier, had 22 points, 9 rebounds and 2 blocked shots in front of 750 fans as Bangor went to 11–0.

Auburndale coach Tim Anderson, a 1963 Bangor graduate, was honored before the game and won his 501st career game in front of a capacity crowd. Bangor led 11–9 after one quarter, but Auburndale (13–0, No. 2 in Division 3) scored the next eight points and pulled away. Troy Bolcerek re-sprained his ankle midway through the second quarter, and Bangor shot 9 for 40 in its first loss.
Troy Bolcerek, hampered by a sprained left ankle, helped Bangor, ranked ninth in Division 4, stay unbeaten in the Scenic Bluffs at 8–0. Danny Sullivan led Wonewoc-Center with 26 points.
Trailing by a point with less than a minute to play, Kyle Schroeder made a steal and a layup, and Bangor escaped to stay unbeaten in the Scenic Bluffs at 9–0.

Troy Bolcerek's 3-pointer at the buzzer won it in overtime. Royall's Sam Overlien hit a fadeaway jumper for a 45–43 lead, the officials put the clock back to three seconds, and Kyle Schroeder's baseball pass found Bolcerek just behind the arc. Royall had tied it 41–41 on an Overlien 3 with 1:45 left in regulation, and Bolcerek scored five of his 19 points in overtime as Bangor went to 10–0 in the Scenic Bluffs.

recap: Troy Bolcerek scored his 1,000th career point in the fourth quarter and led all scorers with 24 points and seven rebounds, as Bangor clinched at least a share of the Scenic Bluffs title. Bangor opened on a 14–2 run, led 37–27 at halftime and by 15 after three quarters.
Troy Bolcerek scored nine points in the second quarter to break open a 15–15 game, and Bangor, ranked seventh in Division 4, led by eight at halftime. Bolcerek had nine rebounds.

Bangor trailed by three at halftime, then Chris Chandler scored six points in the third quarter to break the game open. Hillsboro rallied with four 3-pointers in the fourth, three by Drew Alexander, but Scenic Bluffs champion Bangor held on to go 13–0 in the league. Hillsboro made nine 3-pointers, five by Greg Jefferies. (The paper's quarter scores for Hillsboro add to 54, one more than its final, so its third and fourth quarters are left blank.)

recap: Bangor led 19–17 after one quarter and outscored Cashton 24–15 in the second for a 43–32 halftime lead. Troy Bolcerek scored 27 points with four 3-pointers, and Bangor finished 14–0 in the Scenic Bluffs, the first team to go unbeaten in the conference since Wonewoc-Center in 1992–93.
Bangor, ranked fifth in Division 4 by the Associated Press, led 41–9 at halftime of the WIAA Division 4 regional first round.

Troy Bolcerek scored nine of his 21 points in the first quarter and added six assists and five rebounds, and the top-seeded Cardinals led 31–20 at halftime of the regional semifinal for their 10th straight win.

event: WIAA Division 4 regional final at Wonewoc-Center
recap: Bangor never trailed but struggled from the field and went 4 for 13 from the free-throw line. With 3:29 left, Brandon Meyer made a steal and deflected it to Kyle Schroeder, who scored and was fouled for a 50–45 lead, and Brookwood scored just two more points. Troy Bolcerek scored nine of his 24 points in the fourth quarter as Bangor won the Wonewoc-Center regional.

event: WIAA Division 4 sectional semifinal at La Crosse Central
recap: Blair-Taylor's quick guards, T.J. Nereng (22 points, eight assists) and Josh Peterson, ended Bangor's season at 22–2 in the WIAA Division 4 sectional semifinal, in front of an estimated 1,700 fans at La Crosse Central's Mark Sutton Gymnasium. The Wildcats led 34–28 at halftime. Bangor opened the second half on a 12–2 run, with 3-pointers from Lukas Ermis and Troy Bolcerek, who scored 26, but a 13–3 Blair-Taylor run gave the Wildcats a six-point lead after three quarters, and sophomore Jacob Stephenson scored 20 off Nereng's passes.
